Anatomic Site:Tumor- FS
Posterior margin brain
Tumor brain
Superior margin brain
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of oligoastrocytoma, grade
II, initially resected in 2005, followed by radiotherapy. She
now presents with possible tumor progression.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received in three parts, each labeled with the patient's name
and medical record number. Part A is received
fresh, and Parts B and C are received in formalin.
Part A, labeled "tumor," consists of multiple fragments of
gray-white, soft tissue measuring 1.3 x 0.6 x 0.3 cm in
aggregate. A portion is taken for cytologic preparation. The remainder
of the specimen is entirely submitted for frozen
section diagnosis 1, with the frozen section remnant submitted in cassette A1.
Part B is labeled "posterior margin permanent." It consists of
four unoriented fragments of pink-tan, soft tissue,
measuring 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm in aggregate. The specimen is entirely submitted
in cassette B1.
Part C is labeled "tumor--permanent." It consists of multiple
unoriented fragments of pink-tan, soft tissue,
measuring 2.8 x 1.5 x 0.4 cm in aggregate. The specimen is entirely submitted
in cassette C1.
Diagnosis Comments:
This oligodendroglial neoplasm exhibits a prominent microcystic component,
without identifiable high-grade features.
Immunohistochemical studies conducted in our laboratory show
that the tumor cells are negative for GFAP and IDH1. Staining for p53 is positive in scattered nuclei, and
MIB-1 (ki-67) staining is low. These findings
support the diagnosis of a WHO Grade II Oligodendroglioma. Thus, the
current specimen represents a recurrence of the
neoplasm treated initially in 2005 (s05-23456)
A detailed assessment of MIB-1 labeling index will be conducted and reported in
an addendum.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1  (A) Brain, biopsy:  Infiltrating glioma, no high-grade features
identified. Tissue section and cytologic preparation.
(Dr. Maria Chen, 55321.)
Final Diagnosis:
A.  Brain, right parietal lobe, biopsy:  Infiltrating glioma.
B.  Brain, posterior margin, biopsy:  Cortex and white matter with reactive
changes.
C.  Brain, right parietal lobe, excision: Oligodendroglioma, WHO Grade II; see
comment.
D.  Brain, superior margin, biopsy:  A segment of cortex, white matter and
leptomeninges with reactive changes and a small focus
of oligodendroglioma.

Anatomic Site: Left temporal cortex (FS)
Left temporal subcortical (FS)
Left temporal cortex
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 42-year-old woman who undergoes resection of a left temporal
lobe tumor.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in two parts, each labeled with the patient's
name and medical record number.
Part A, additionally labeled "left temporal cortex," consists of a single,
unoriented, friable fragment of gray, soft tissue
measuring 1.6 x 1.2 x 0.4 cm. A small portion is used for cytologic prep. The
remaining specimen is submitted in its entirety in
cassette A1.
Part B, additionally labeled "left temporal subcortical," consists of multiple
unoriented fragments of gray, soft tissue
measuring 1.1 x 0.9 x 0.5 cm in aggregate. A small portion is used for
cytologic prep. The remaining specimen is submitted in
its entirety in cassette B1.
Part C is additionally labeled "left temporal cortex." It consists of a
72.5-gm piece of cerebral cortex measuring 6.8 x 6.5 x
3.3 cm. Representative sections of the specimen are submitted in cassettes
C1-C12.
Diagnosis Comments:
The specimen demonstrates an infiltrative glial neoplasm with both astrocytic
and oligodendroglial elements, approximately
equally represented. The tumor is hypercellular, with marked nuclear
pleomorphism and readily-identifiable mitoses. There is
no evidence of necrosis or microvascular proliferation.
The preliminary diagnosis was discussed at the UCLA Neuro-Oncology Tumor Board
on 12/15/06. The preliminary diagnosis was
discussed with Dr. Taylor on 12/15/06.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
A. Brain, left temporal cortex, biopsy: Consistent with a diffuse
astrocytoma (WHO grade III). Cannot exclude mixed
oligoastrocytoma with an astrocytic predominance. Cytologic preparation only.
 (Dr. Emily R. Johnson, 48721.)
B. Brain, left temporal subcortical, biopsy: Consistent with a diffuse
astrocytoma (WHO grade III). Cannot exclude mixed
oligoastrocytoma with an astrocytic predominance. Cytologic preparation only.
 (Dr. Emily R. Johnson, 48721.)
Final Diagnosis:
A. Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Anaplastic oligoastrocytoma, WHO grade
III; see comment.
B. Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Anaplastic oligoastrocytoma, WHO grade
III; see comment.
C. Brain, left temporal lobe, resection: Anaplastic oligoastrocytoma, WHO
grade III; see comment.
